g.text: The link: two stations, the air between, and the time it takes

Quantum position verification: a verifier sends a 2-bit basis, the prover measures and answers 1-2 bits; what matters is that the answer leaves the instant the measurement is done. The radio adds a fixed ~23 ns to each hop.
with the verifier's carrier in T/R mode)
over the air: 5.8 GHz (4.9-5.875 GHz in spec), each direction its own frequency (two antennas) or the same one in turns (one antenna + switch)
path loss: 68 dB at 10 m, 97 dB at 300 m, 134 dB at 20 km (free space)
flight time 3.34 ns per metre: 33 ns across the lab, 1 µs across campus, 67 µs to a mountain 20 km away
with 24 dBi panels both ends and no amplifier: -76 dBm at 20 km (SNR 16 dB in 100 MHz; the slow path confirms from 20 dB further)

text.style: fill: #444444; font: italic 6.5px 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle

g.text: FPGA ↔ board: 3.3 V CMOS on the 40-pin header
TX: 4 ladder bits; RX: 3 comparator lines
+ SPI, I2C, HOLD, SEL, TRIG, T/R
CMP_I on pin 18 and TRIG_IN on 26 are
The round trip, in nanoseconds (10 m across the lab)
RX electronics to the prover's register
prover decides, measures, answers (the quantity under test)
RX electronics to the verifier's register

Electronics per hop: 23.5 ns on the PYNQ-Z2 (8.8 ns of it is the PYNQ's 200 Ω header resistors, twice), 14.7 ns on the Icepi Zero; sim/budget.py section 5 itemises it. The old OOK link budgeted 10-100 ns for its envelope detector.
In one-antenna T/R mode each station's switch adds 30 ns (HMC536) before it can answer; a 1 µs switch (SKY13453) would be 15 round trips of the lab.
TWO ANTENNAS PER LINK, TWO FREQUENCIES (full duplex)
• this is what the board does with nothing added: TX ANT and RX ANT
• both carriers on all the time: both loops locked, no holds, no turnaround
• TX→RX isolation needed in the same band: 60-70 dB (sim/budget.py §4), which two panels side by side (~40 dB) plus 600 MHz of separation (the arm filter's 31 dB) give
• the four panels = one link, exactly
• 3 directions: 6 panels, 6 channels; with the arm filter at 50 MHz they fit 5.15-5.85 GHz
ONE ANTENNA PER DIRECTION, SAME FREQUENCY, IN TURNS (T/R, half duplex)
• the on-board HMC536 block: ANT, SW TX, SW RX jacks, TR_A/TR_B from the FPGA
• 30 ns to switch, 27 dB isolation, +29 dBm; the far loop HOLDs while we transmit
• the reply carrier must already be on frequency: REF OUT → REF IN makes the prover a coherent transponder (its TX synthesizer runs on the VCXO the loop steers)
• with a PA: a limiter ahead of the LNA (0 dBm leaks through the switch at +27 dBm)
• 3 directions: 3 panels, 3 channels (or 1 channel if the schedule never overlaps)
• each link needs ~200 MHz (the ±100 MHz arm filter) to be deaf to its neighbour by 14 dB, 600 MHz to be deaf by 31 dB
• the usable span 5.15-5.875 GHz is 725 MHz: three or four 200 MHz channels, six at 100 MHz spacing with a 50 MHz arm filter (+3.5 ns)

• ISM 5.725-5.875 alone holds one link; the UNII bands (5.15-5.725) the others — DFS radar-detection rules apply to 5.25-5.725 for licensed-exempt gear; an amateur licence (5.65-5.925 GHz, 5 cm band) is the clean way to run the PAs
• beyond that, it is the switch again: time division at 30 ns
